source_review.notes: Checked all thirteen primary or project-authoritative references. Current CNCF Platforms guidance supports platforms as integrated user-defined capability collections, platform-as-product, consistent interfaces, self-service, reduced cognitive load, optional/composable use, secure defaults, thin provider layers, user research, and outcome-oriented measurement. The CNCF maturity model treats people, process, policy, technology, and outcomes as contextual dimensions rather than one checkbox level. DORA 2024 supports user-centeredness, developer independence, product mindset, and mixed survey associations rather than guaranteed causal improvement. Current Backstage documentation supports component/API/resource/system/owner catalog modeling, templates with tasks and review, and permission controls. OpenGitOps supports declarative, versioned/immutable, automatically pulled, continuously reconciled desired state. NIST SSDF supports integrating secure-development practices into the SDLC. Kubernetes API conventions and OpenTelemetry specifications support durable operation/status semantics and correlated telemetry.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and offers no deductive proof; its assurance chain is conditional on user evidence, organizational ownership, provider behavior, policy, operations, measurement, and decisions.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; journey success and value formulas are sample and decision models with stated attribution, unit, uncertainty, representativeness, and causal limitations.

evidence: The executable pilot scorecard is labeled synthetic internal decision evidence and explicitly disclaims outcome and causal proof.
The ten portal, tool, scaffold, interface, adoption, escape, outage, metric, provider, and stop examples are scenarios rather than observations.
DORA population survey findings are labeled associations that motivate hypotheses rather than organization-specific causal predictions.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production platform, user study, task attempt, policy decision, deployment, incident, support record, cost saving, adoption result, business outcome, or retirement result is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently distinguishes MVP from demo, minimum scope from minimum quality, platform from portal/substrate, capability from provider, cohort from fleet, self-service from no support, golden path from mandate, accepted from ready, catalog projection from authority, adoption from value, association from causation, control-plane availability from workload continuity, and deletion from retirement.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can research a cohort/job, baseline the complete journey, map ownership, select a vertical slice, define capability/provider contracts, unify identity/state/interfaces, build secure and operable paths, preserve escape and recovery routes, run a real pilot, evaluate balanced evidence and cost, and expand, pivot, or retire against declared criteria.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from MVP definition and cohort discovery through baseline/value stream, vertical scope, contracts, identity/API/golden paths, security/reconciliation, operations/failure/optionality, measurement/economics, criteria, pilot, and evolution. Ten examples cover portal-only inventory, tool-first scope, incomplete templates, interface drift, coerced adoption, escape paths, control-plane coupling, vanity signals, provider reuse, and disciplined stopping. Five exercises progress from definitions through journey mapping, adversarial redesign, regulated architecture, and a mixed-evidence decision, with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
